# Official Statements on Free-Threaded Python Performance Impact

Based on official CPython documentation and PEPs, here are the key statements about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build:

## Performance Overhead

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "The performance penalty on linear performance, comparing a free-threaded build against a with-GIL build, as measured by the pyperformance benchmarks (for example as run by Microsoft's Faster CPython team, or Meta's Python Runtime team), is currently around 10% (except on macOS, where it's more like 3%)." | CLAIM: The free-threaded build currently has approximately 10% performance overhead compared to the GIL build on most platforms, but only 3% on macOS.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: Official documentation states the single-threaded performance overhead varies by platform, ranging from 1% to 8%.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The changes to make CPython thread-safe without the GIL increase execution overhead for `--disable-gil` builds." | CLAIM: The original PEP acknowledges that removing the GIL introduces performance overhead.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "Note that this PEP would not affect the performance of the default (non `--disable-gil`) builds of CPython." | CLAIM: The performance impact is isolated to the free-threaded build only; the default GIL-enabled build remains unaffected.

## Acceptable Performance Targets

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "The Steering Council mentioned they expected free-threaded Python to be around 10-15% slower, although this was not a hard target." | CLAIM: The Python Steering Council considers 10-15% overhead acceptable for the free-threaded build.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "We are currently around 10% and don't expect it to get slower, but for phase II (not the default flip), we propose 15% as a hard performance target." | CLAIM: The proposed maximum acceptable overhead is 15% for making free-threaded Python officially supported (phase II).

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075 | QUOTE: "At this point we're expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council's worst-case expectation is a 10-15% performance penalty.

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075 | QUOTE: "We don't want to set strict limits on acceptable performance, partly because we don't want to get stuck in arguments about how to measure performance and partly because it will depend on user expectations." | CLAIM: The Steering Council deliberately avoids setting strict performance limits.

## Memory Impact

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "Exact numbers vary because of the different gc module implementation, but free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)." | CLAIM: The free-threaded build uses 15-20% more memory than the GIL-enabled build.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build will typically use more memory compared to the default build." | CLAIM: Official documentation confirms higher memory usage is expected in free-threaded builds.

## Future Optimizations

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "We have a few more PRs in flight that should get us comfortably below 10% on Linux and Windows." | CLAIM: Developers are actively working on optimizations to reduce overhead below 10% on major platforms.

## Summary

The Python Software Foundation and CPython developers officially acknowledge:
- **CPU overhead**: Currently 8-10% on most platforms (1-3% on macOS), with a target of keeping it under 15%
- **Memory overhead**: 15-20% higher memory usage
- **Scope**: Impact is isolated to the free-threaded build only; default builds are unaffected
- **Ongoing work**: Active development to reduce overhead further

The performance cost is considered acceptable given the benefits of true parallel execution on multi-core systems.
